not_my_life.research: premise does not fit (Sally 前提不符)

flow: chapters 1 to 7, in order, each opened by its title and intro
teen run (setup.age = teen): locked18 cards are never shown; teenPrompt replaces prompt where present
C3-9 shows only if the C3-8 picks include a T11A line (gateRule)
a feeling card always plays right after the card named in follows
after chapter 7: node score.mjs profile; for any axis marked unfinished, play up to 2 extras with axisFor = that axis, then profile again
node score.mjs freeze (sha256 shown before the finale)

chapters.title: Your phone
chapters.intro: Your phone already knows too much about you. I just want the highlights.

cards.prompt: The main group chat is at 99+ unread. Be honest. In there, you're the…

options.t: Planner. Makes the poll. Nobody votes. Decides anyway.
Recruiter. "Everyone, this is Sam. Be nice."
Courier. Screenshots the good stuff straight to my two favorites.
Ghost. Reads everything, says nothing, still shows up Saturday.
Scorekeeper. Knows exactly who didn't react to MY message.
Lawyer. "Okay, but have we heard THEIR side?"

cards.mask: looks like a group chat meme; measures circle size (T04: Close Friends list vs Mayor of every group chat), how much contact you need to see (T02, slight on both sides), and, slightly, running things by structure (T24A) and giving the accused a hearing (T08A)

friend.prompt: In the main group chat, {name} is the one who…

a.t: Adds new people: "Everyone, this is Sam."

b.t: Screenshots it all to two favorites.

cards.prompt: Your person, totally casual: "Let's swap passcodes. Nothing's wrong. It just feels close." They're already holding their phone out.
cards.teenPrompt: Your best friend, totally casual: "Let's swap passcodes. Besties do." They're already holding their phone out.

options.t: Type mine into their phone before they finish the sentence.
Point out we already did. Two years ago. They forgot.
Offer a trade: my photos, yes. My DMs, never.
Keep mine. "Nothing to hide. Still no."
Laugh, change the subject, hope it never comes back.
Not my call. Parents or work set my phone rules.

cards.mask: looks like a phone privacy question; measures whether closeness means sharing everything or keeping your own door (R1) and phone openness (T01)

friend.prompt: {name}'s person suggests swapping phone passcodes. Nothing's wrong. What does {name} do?

a.t: Swaps on the spot.

b.t: Keeps {their} own: "Nothing to hide. Still no."

cards.prompt: Last time something was eating at you after midnight, where did it go first?

options.t: Typed it all out to an AI. It asked good questions.
Voice-noted my closest person. Four minutes, no summary.
Posted a sad song on my story. Waited to see who'd ask.
Notes app. A whole essay nobody will ever read.
Nowhere. Stared at the ceiling till 3am. Told no one.

cards.mask: looks like a late-night habit; measures whether an AI counts as a real confidant or your own raw words do (T03: the voice note and the Notes-app essay are the no-AI routes) and whether you wait to be reached (T02B). Tag-only, like Sally's Q44: no axis. 'Nowhere' is a circumstance: nothing went anywhere, so there is no choice to score

friend.prompt: Something's eating at {name} after midnight. Where does it go first?

a.t: Typed out to an AI.

b.t: A long voice note to {their} closest person.

cards.prompt: Your whole friend group joins a new map app: everyone's dot, battery and song, live. Now the popup wants your location.

options.t: Always. Come find me. I'm the dot at 4%.
Share it with my top three. Everyone else can guess.
Allow it, then revoke it at 2am after one scary video.
Freeze my dot at home. Technically sharing.

cards.mask: looks like an app permission popup; measures whether you let your people see where you are, always on, or keep your dot to yourself (T01, Sally Q42 reframed to location with your close people), and, slightly, a tiny inner circle (T04A)

friend.prompt: {name}'s friends all join an app that shares everyone's location. What does {name} pick?

a.t: Always. Come find me.

b.t: Freezes {their} dot at home. Technically sharing.

cards.prompt: You and an old close friend haven't texted in four months. Nobody's mad. You still love them.

options.t: Send a random pic, no hello. Like we never stopped.
Like their story. Let them take it from there.

cards.mask: looks like a friendship hot take; measures whether a quiet friendship still feels safe or needs the other person to reach out first (T02). Options are moves (text like no time passed, or wait for their text), not feelings, so they no longer restate C1-11's golden answers

friend.prompt: {name} and an old close friend haven't texted in four months. What does {name} do?

a.t: Sends a random pic, no hello, like they never stopped.

b.t: Waits. The last text was {name}'s.

cards.prompt: You owe someone a real apology. You know exactly what you mean. AI could word it way better.

options.t: Let AI fix it. Add one typo so it sounds like me.
Send my own version. It took 40 minutes and says sorry six times.

cards.mask: looks like a tech opinion; measures whether sincerity lives in the intent and follow-through or in your own raw words (T03); the long own-words apology is also slight love-in-words evidence (T05B, library Q43 trigger)

friend.prompt: {name} owes someone a real apology. AI could word it better. What does {name} send?

a.t: The AI version, plus one fake typo.

b.t: {Their} own version. 40 minutes, six sorries.

cards.prompt: Someone you talked to for four minutes at a party sends you a follow request.

options.t: Accept and follow back. We're basically friends now.
Leave it pending. Forever.

cards.mask: looks like a social media reflex; measures how wide you let your circle go (T04)

friend.prompt: Someone {name} met for four minutes at a party sends a follow request. What does {name} do?

a.t: Accepts and follows back.

b.t: Leaves it pending forever.

cards.prompt: Think of the last time a message that mattered showed "Read" and no reply.

options.t: Forgot about it. They'd answer eventually.
Kept checking if they'd been online since.
Reread my message like it was evidence.
Handed my best friend my phone: "Write the follow-up. Make it chill."
Turned off my own read receipts. Forever.

cards.mask: looks like a texting moment; measures whether silence after a message that mattered feels fine or needs checking (T02, did-grade) and, slightly, how open your phone is to your people: hand it to a friend to write the follow-up (T01A) or lock down what others can see (T01B). Golden card (BRIEF.md golden set), the three golden options unchanged

friend.prompt: Last time a message that mattered to {name} showed "Read" and got no reply, {they}...

a.t: Forgot about it. A reply would come eventually.

b.t: Kept checking when the other person was last online.

chapters.title: Friends
chapters.intro: Your friends have seen your 2am face. Now it's my turn.

cards.prompt: Your friend plays you a song they wrote for a contest. Entries close at midnight. It's not good. They look so hopeful.

options.t: "The chorus needs work. Want notes before midnight?"
"This is a hit." Start humming it on the spot.
Rave about the verse. Mumble "maybe a louder chorus?" Change the subject.
"Honestly? Enter the other song you played me."

cards.mask: looks like a music moment; measures saying the hard thing now versus holding the person first (R2) and plain versus wrapped delivery (T07)

friend.prompt: A friend plays {name} their contest song. Entries close at midnight. It's not good. What does {name} do?

a.t: Says the chorus needs work and offers notes.

b.t: Calls it a hit and hums along.

cards.prompt: Your most recent "wait, this costs HOW much?" plan from a friend. A birthday dinner, a concert, a trip.

options.t: Went, paid, and ate instant noodles for a week.
Admitted it was over my budget in the chat. Took three drafts.
Paid my share. Home by 9. Completely peopled out.
Invented a clash. Sent a very long, very sweet message instead.

cards.mask: looks like a money story; measures stretching for your people versus guarding your own energy (T06) and showing up in deeds versus in words (T05: going and paying, or the long sweet message instead). Capacity card: scores no R2 by design. Money limits never score (T06B never: not having the money): admitting it was over budget is the circumstance option; T06B comes only from the paid-then-home-by-9 line (paying first shows the limit is energy, not money)

friend.prompt: Last time a friend's plan cost way more than {name} wanted to spend, {they}...

a.t: Went, paid, and lived on noodles after.

b.t: Paid {their} share, then was home by 9. Peopled out.

cards.prompt: The person who started a rumor about your friend last year wants back in the group chat. They apologized. Publicly. With a slideshow. They've been decent ever since.

options.t: Add them back. Break the ice with a meme.
One group hangout first. I'm watching the whole time.
DM my friend: "Say the word and I hit decline."
Say yes. Keep the old screenshots, just in case.
Depends what the rumor actually was.

cards.mask: looks like group chat politics; measures belief in second chances versus protecting the person who got hurt (T08)

friend.prompt: The person who started a rumor about {name}'s friend apologized, publicly, and has been decent since. Now they want back in the group chat. {name}...

a.t: Adds them back right away.

b.t: Tells the friend: say the word and it's a no.

cards.prompt: Your friend just got dumped, out of nowhere. Pick the two moves you'd actually make.

options.t: Show up with snacks: "They were mid anyway."
Send a voice note listing why they're amazing. Numbered.
Rally the whole group out tonight. Nobody sits home.
Just us two, their couch, their comfort show.
Make them a playlist with a note on every song.
Block the ex on their phone for them. With permission. Mostly.

cards.mask: looks like breakup first aid; measures love shown in deeds versus in words (T05) and a small versus a big circle (T04); the unedited voice note is also slight own-words evidence (T03B, library call 'You'd rather send a voice note than let anything tidy up what you meant')

friend.prompt: {name}'s friend just got dumped out of nowhere. {name}...

a.t: Shows up with snacks and trashes the ex.

b.t: Sends a numbered voice note on why they're amazing.

cards.prompt: 11:48pm. You're finally drifting off. Your best friend texts: "are you up? it's the talking-stage drama again, sorry." Third night this week.

options.t: Sit straight up and call. Sleep is canceled.
Pretend I'm asleep. Text them first thing at 7am.
"They're the WORST. Love you. Sleeping." Phone goes across the room.
Call, put them on speaker, "mhm" until one of us sleeps.
Heart the text. Phone face down. Actually asleep.

cards.mask: looks like a late-night text; measures giving past empty versus charging yourself first (T06). Capacity card: scores no R2 by design. The drama is named so it reads as no danger (Sally Q27 premise, teen-safe)

friend.prompt: 11:48pm, third night this week, {name}'s best friend texts "are you up?" about the same talking-stage drama. {name}...

a.t: Sits straight up and calls. Sleep is canceled.

b.t: Plays asleep and texts back at 7am.

cards.prompt: Remember the last time a friend was clearly in the wrong with someone else? A mean joke, a nasty comment, a pile-on.

options.t: Told them straight it was wrong. Left on read for two days.
Took them for bubble tea first. Brought it up on the walk back.
Stayed on my friend's side. Never brought it up.
Said nothing to my friend. Checked on the other person.
Laughed along, then felt weird about it all day.

cards.mask: looks like a drama recap; measures whether you say the hard thing to a friend in the wrong or hold them first (R2, did-grade tie breaker). Looking after the hurt person feeds T08B, not R2; laughing along is a circumstance (swept along in the moment, not a stance): it scores nothing and is logged with its guilt

friend.prompt: Last time a friend of {name}'s was clearly in the wrong with someone, {they}...

a.t: Told the friend straight that it was wrong.

b.t: Took the friend for bubble tea first, raised it later.

cards.prompt: Rewind to that moment. First feeling, no editing.

options.t: Cringe. Full-body cringe.
Angry, on the other person's behalf.
Worried I'd get dragged into it.
Guilty. Part of me found it funny.
A sting. My friend wasn't who I thought.

cards.mask: looks like a vibe check; logs the emotion under the friend-in-the-wrong memory (emotion only, no profile evidence), so 'kept quiet but was furious' can surface as a split

cards.prompt: Your close friend's laptop died a week before a big deadline. They need $300 by Friday, no idea when they can pay you back. You have it. Losing it would sting.
cards.teenPrompt: Your close friend's laptop died a week before exams. They need $60 toward a used one by Friday, no idea when they'll pay you back. You have it. Losing it would sting.

options.t: Send it tonight. Sort out paying back whenever.
Lend them my old laptop. "One crumb in the keys and it's war."
Start a laptop fund in the group chat. Put in first.
Agree on a payback date first. Set a reminder titled "OWED".
Can't. Having it isn't the same as having it spare.

cards.mask: looks like a money favor; measures stretching for your people (T06: send it, or rally the group and go first), keeping things square (T12) and love by roast plus deed (T05A: lending your own laptop with a threat). Four different moves, no amounts ladder

friend.prompt: {name}'s close friend needs money fast and can't say when they'll pay it back. {name}...

a.t: Sends it tonight, payback whenever.

b.t: Agrees on a payback date first and sets a reminder.

cards.prompt: The whole group got invited to a party Saturday. Except one friend. They just asked the chat: "anything fun this weekend?" In your group, you're the...

options.t: Truth-teller: "There's a party. You're not on the list. Sorry."
Leaker: Forwards them the invite. "Just thought you should know."
Cover story: "Dead weekend, sadly." Then posts zero stories all night.
Smuggler: "Come with me. Act like you were invited."
Plan B: "Eh, some party. Their loss. Mini golf Saturday, loser pays."

cards.mask: looks like group chat drama; measures saying the hard thing to a friend now versus protecting them first (R2) and plain versus cushioned delivery (T07). Hard news about the friend's place in the group, not their work, look or story, so it no longer repeats C2-1 or C3-12 ('your friend's thing isn't good'). The cover story is a kind lie, so it scores Soft but no T07B (T07B never: dishonest). Round 2: no hint-and-change-the-subject line and no tell-them-later-over-food line, so the answer set no longer mirrors C2-1 and C2-5. The smuggler says the exclusion out loud and overrides it (R2 +1, no tag); Plan B breaks the news now but wraps it in a consolation plan (R2 -1, T07B s1)

friend.prompt: {name}'s whole group got invited to a party. One friend didn't, and asks the chat what's on this weekend. {name} is the...

a.t: Truth-teller: "There's a party. You're not on the list."

b.t: Cover story: "Dead weekend, sadly."

chapters.title: Love and your person
chapters.intro: Your person can be a crush, a partner or your closest friend. I just want the gossip.

cards.prompt: Think back, or ahead. Three months of talking every single day. Tonight, mid-snack, they look up: 'So... what are we?'

options.t: 'Obviously. We're official. I'm changing my bio.'
'Do we need a label? I like what this is.'
'Official, sure. But no anniversaries and no couple pics.'
Skip the talk. Book the meet-my-family dinner for Sunday.

cards.mask: looks like a cute crush moment; measures R3, the classic relationship script (the label, the family intro) versus writing your own

friend.prompt: Someone {name} has talked to every day for three months asks, 'So... what are we?' {name} would...

a.t: Make it official. Bio updated, family dinner booked.

b.t: 'Do we need a label? I like what this is.'

cards.prompt: Remember the last party or big hangout you and your person walked into together? Crush, partner or closest friend counts.

options.t: Stuck together all night. Basically one person with two phones.
Split up at the door. Met at the end to swap gossip.
Left early together. The walk home was the best part.
Introduced them to everyone. Then abandoned them by the chips.

cards.mask: looks like party gossip; measures R1 in a real, recent moment: together as a unit versus two people who each have their own night

friend.prompt: {name} walks into a party with a crush, partner or best friend. Where is {name} an hour later?

a.t: Glued together. Same corner, same snacks.

b.t: Off with other friends. Gossip swap at the end.

cards.prompt: You move in with your person. They earn twice what you do. Rent, groceries, Wi-Fi, the fancy olive oil. How does it get split?
cards.teenPrompt: You and your best friend plan a day out: train, bubble tea, arcade. They get twice your allowance. How does it get split?

options.t: 50/50. I'll just buy the cheaper version of everything.
By what each of us has, so it pinches us the same.
Payment request for every single thing. Itemized.
One shared pot. Neither of us checks the balance.
Whatever I can cover that month. Some months that's not half.

cards.mask: looks like bill logistics; measures whether fair means the same amount (T12A) or the same weight on each person (T12B)

friend.prompt: {name} moves in with someone who earns twice as much. How does {name} want the bills split?

a.t: 50/50, even if it pinches {name} more.

b.t: By income, so it pinches both the same.

cards.prompt: Think of the last time someone close kept grating on you for weeks. Small stuff: lateness, dishes, texting habits. Nobody was the villain.

options.t: Sat them down and made an actual deal.
Let it fade. No fight, just fewer plans.
Ended it with a kind text I rewrote eleven times.
Joked about it until they finally got the hint.
Started doing their dishes too, and mentioned it. Often.

cards.mask: looks like a pet-peeve story; measures whether a no-fault misfit gets repaired (T10A) or is reason enough to step back (T10B), Sally Q08

friend.prompt: Months of small clashes with someone close, nobody at fault. {name} would...

a.t: Make a deal and give it time.

b.t: Call it. Not a fit is reason enough.

cards.prompt: You find out your person has spent months in late-night chats with someone else. Inside jokes, secrets they used to tell only you. Nothing physical. What hurts most?
cards.teenPrompt: Your best friend has spent months in late-night chats with someone new. Inside jokes, secrets they used to tell only you. They never mentioned it. What hurts most?

options.t: The secrets. That closeness was supposed to be ours.
The months. How many times did they look me in the eye?
That we never set rules. I can't even be mad properly.
Envy. Someone else got the good version of them.

cards.mask: looks like a betrayal story; measures whether the wound is lost emotional exclusivity (T09A) or the lying and the never-agreed deal (T09B), Sally Q06

cards.prompt: A friend's toddler falls asleep on you mid-party. Nobody can move you for an hour. Pick the two thoughts closest to yours.

options.t: I want one. My parents would be unbearable grandparents.
I already have names picked out.
Someday. After I can keep a plant alive.
Cute. Anyway, my life plan has zero car seats.
Is a dog basically the same thing? Asking for me.
I'd want this, but my life can't fit it now.

cards.mask: looks like a sweet party moment; measures how you feel about being a parent someday (Sally Q10, T11): the plain want and the plain no carry s2, the maybe-later line s1, with a circumstance line for want-but-can't

cards.prompt: Your person's last joke about you that landed a little too hard, in front of everyone. Your singing, your cooking, your middle school photos. What did you do?

options.t: Said it right there: 'Okay, that one actually hurt.'
Roasted them right back, twice as hard. Now we're even.
Went quiet until they asked what was wrong.
Laughed it off. They meant well, and they were having fun.

cards.mask: looks like a roast story; measures R2 on a real card outside chapter 2: saying the hurt out loud to your person versus protecting their moment. You are the target here, so it does not repeat the 'your friend's thing isn't good' cards (C2-1, C2-8, C2-10)

friend.prompt: {name}'s person makes a joke about {name} in front of everyone, and it stings. {name}...

a.t: Says it right there: 'Okay, that one hurt.'

b.t: Laughs it off. They meant well.

cards.gate: Show only if the player picked a T11A line on C3-8 (Sally: Q11 only for those who lean toward wanting kids on Q10).
cards.prompt: Kids are penciled in for the next two years. There's already a nursery mood board. Then your dream job calls: bigger title, new city, answer by Friday.

options.t: Turn it down. The mood board stays on schedule.
Take it. We push the baby plan back a year.
Take it. The mood board was always more their dream.
Depends. Whichever one we'd regret more.

options: The job won't come around again.
My person's career needs the room too.
My parents can help with the baby.

cards.mask: looks like a timing puzzle; measures whether a wanted family plan bends for a career win (Sally Q11, T11A), with L2 as slight evidence and a slight T11B line for the player whose kid plan was never really theirs

cards.prompt: You and your person, on a normal week. Pick the two lines most like you.

options.t: If they're free, I'm suddenly free too.
Some nights I'm offline, and they know not to ask.
We take turns paying. I always know whose turn it is.
I have a hobby they've never tried and never will.
They get a play-by-play of my day. Photos of lunch included.
Whoever just got paid covers food. That's the whole system.

cards.mask: looks like cute relationship habits; measures R1, most free time shared versus close with your own time and interests kept (Sally Q05), plus one slight line each for keeping exact turns (T12A) and whoever has more pays (T12B)

friend.prompt: On a normal week with a partner or closest friend, {name} would rather...

a.t: Share every free evening and narrate the whole day.

b.t: Keep some nights solo, no explaining needed.

chapters.title: Money and treats
chapters.intro: Money talk. No judgment. Okay, a little judgment.

cards.prompt: You find $200 in a jacket you haven't worn since last winter.

options.t: Concert tickets. Tonight if possible.
Straight into savings. Future me says thanks.
Dinner for my people. Found money gets shared.
It went to a bill. Romance is dead.

cards.mask: looks like a lucky find; measures whether spare money becomes an experience now or a cushion for later (L1, T13), with slight generosity (T06A)

friend.prompt: {name} finds $200 in an old jacket. Where does it go?

a.t: Concert tickets, tonight.

b.t: Straight into savings.

cards.prompt: Confession time. The last time you wanted one more of something you already own plenty of. Tote bags, figures, skins, mugs. What did you do?

options.t: Bought it on the spot. There's always room for one more.
Cleared out a few old ones first, then bought it.
Left it in my cart for a week. The feeling passed.
Bought it, then hid the bag for a few days.

cards.mask: looks like a shopping confession; measures whether a full collection limits a new treat (Sally Q36, T14, did-grade)

friend.prompt: {name} already owns plenty of tote bags and spots a new one to love. What happens?

a.t: Buys it on the spot.

b.t: Clears out old ones first.

cards.prompt: Money memes that might be about you. Which two are painfully accurate?

options.t: I have a savings goal with a name.
I've booked something before checking my balance.
I've watched a 'broke to six figures' video. Twice. Took notes.
Everything under $20 counts as basically free.
I could tell you what I spent on boba last month.
My fun money is gone by the 10th. Somehow.

cards.mask: looks like a money meme list; measures save versus leap (L1, T13), believing effort pays (T15A) and track versus feel (T24), each slight. Fix pass round 2 dropped the head-start line (C4-2 and C4-7 already carry T15B) so the hot take is not asked twice in three cards

cards.prompt: A plant for your room. $10 at the big store, or $25 from a neighbor whose sales fund the animal shelter.

options.t: The neighbor's. My plant has a backstory now.
The $10 one. The plant can't tell the difference.

cards.mask: looks like a price check; measures paying clearly more so a purchase helps someone versus budget first (Sally Q35 reframed, T23)

friend.prompt: {name} can buy a plant for $10, or for $25 from a neighbor raising money for the animal shelter. Which?

a.t: The neighbor's plant.

b.t: The $10 one.

cards.prompt: Housewarming tour. Your friend pats the kitchen island: 'I worked so hard for this.' Their parents covered the down payment.
cards.teenPrompt: Your friend's parents paid for a private coach all year. They made the team and say, 'I earned this spot.'

options.t: 'You earned it!' I say, and mean it.
Must be nice. Somebody had to say it.

cards.mask: looks like a hot take on a friend; measures whether you credit the effort or name the family head start (Sally Q13, T15). Strength 3 both sides: this is the one card that asks Q13 head on

friend.prompt: A friend whose parents helped a lot says 'I worked so hard for this.' What does {name} think?

a.t: 'You earned it!' And means it.

b.t: Must be nice.

cards.prompt: Two pairs of sneakers. Both comfy, both built to last, both in budget. The pair you love costs $80 more. You've watched 11 unboxing videos of it.

options.t: Buy them. I've already worn them in my head.
The other pair. The 11 videos were the fun part.

cards.mask: looks like a shopping choice; measures paying for the version you love versus the one that does the same job (Sally Q34, T14)

friend.prompt: {name} can afford either pair of sneakers. The favorite pair costs $80 more. Which one?

a.t: The favorite pair.

b.t: The cheaper pair that does the same job.

cards.prompt: Your team's fundraiser wraps. You pick the MVP, and $100 comes with it. Kai raised the most with one post to 40k followers. Remy raised almost as much, door to door.
cards.teenPrompt: Your club's fundraiser wraps. You pick the MVP, and a $50 gift card comes with it. Kai raised the most with one post to 4k followers. Remy raised almost as much, door to door.

options.t: Kai. Most raised wins. Those followers didn't build themselves.
Remy. Kai posted once. The followers did the rest.
Whoever's broke this month gets it. Kai will survive.
Put it to a vote. Majority wins, even if I sulk.

cards.mask: looks like picking an MVP; measures crediting the result (T15A) versus spotting the head start behind it (T15B), with an award by need (T12B) and a fair-process exit (L3). Sally Q16 reframed in fix pass round 2 (reward the result or look at what made it) so it no longer reads as splitting money and never repeats C3-3's equal-versus-proportional split

friend.prompt: {name} picks the fundraiser MVP. Kai raised the most with one post to 40k followers. Remy raised almost as much, door to door. Who gets it?

a.t: Kai. Most raised wins.

b.t: Remy. The followers did Kai's work.

chapters.title: Work, school and ambition
chapters.intro: Grades, shifts, big dreams. Let's see what you're actually working for.

cards.prompt: Genii can spoil your whole future right now. Every school, every job, every win, every plot twist. One tap.

options.t: Spoil it. I'd sleep so much better knowing.
Don't you dare. Finding out is the fun part.

cards.mask: looks like a spoiler joke; measures the need for a locked-in path versus keeping the future open (T17, L2 certainty side)

friend.prompt: Genii offers to spoil {name}'s whole future in one tap. What would {they} say?

a.t: Spoil it. Right now.

b.t: Don't you dare.

cards.prompt: Your boss lets you pick your next assignment. One you've done five times and could do half-asleep. Or one nobody on the team has ever tried.
cards.teenPrompt: Next year you get one elective. The sequel to the class you aced, same teacher. Or a brand-new one nobody at school has taken yet.

options.t: The one I could do half-asleep. Surprises are for birthdays.
The brand-new one. Day one, I'm googling everything.
The safe one. One bad review or grade and I'm done.

cards.mask: looks like picking your next assignment or class; measures the sure thing versus the untried (L1) with a new-versus-familiar read (T22). Rewritten in the fix pass so it no longer repeats C5-6's safe-pay-versus-passion fork
